conditions: The Document’s authorized terms specify a proxy that can decide which future versions may be used.
That proxy publicly accepts the version for election under the governing arrangement.
limitations: The actual work notice establishes whether there is a proxy and the scope of its authority.
Section 10 treats numbered or-later terms and terms without a version number separately. The illustrative Addendum and SPDX catalog tags do not establish a particular work’s grant.

triggers: GNU corrects the registered edition or issues controlling clarification on a cited clause.
The source representation, work-notice assumptions, or exact scope of this proposition changes.

statement: GNU FDL 1.3 section 10 provides that when a covered Document specifies a proxy to decide which future GNU FDL versions may be used, that proxy’s public statement accepting a version permanently authorizes licensees to choose that version for the Document.
